title: The Balanced-Bipartition Extremal Construction Attains n²/12 Monochromatic Triangles (Erdős #76)

problemStatement.formal: \text{For } n = 2m,\ \text{let } c_\star \text{ color } K_n \text{ blue within each half } A,B\ (|A|=|B|=m) \text{ and red between them. Then } \mathrm{maxPackingSize}(c_\star) = (\tfrac{1}{12}+o(1))\,n^2,\ \text{attained by two blue Steiner-triple packings of } K_m \sqcup K_m \text{ (red } K_{m,m} \text{ triangle-free).}
problemStatement.plain: Split the vertices of the complete graph into two equal halves; color edges inside a half blue and edges between halves red. The red edges form a complete bipartite graph, which has no triangle, so every packed monochromatic triangle must be blue and lie entirely inside one half. Each half is a K_{n/2}, which a Steiner triple system tiles into about C(n/2,2)/3 edge-disjoint triangles. Two halves give twice that, totaling about n²/12 — showing this simple coloring reaches the true optimum of Erdős #76.
whyMatters: Certifies that the Gruslys–Letzter lower bound n²/12 is best possible: some coloring actually attains it, so no coloring is forced to have more monochromatic triangles.
Explains why the trivial n²/6 edge-budget (parent entry) is halved — the extremal coloring wastes one whole color class on a triangle-free bipartite subgraph.
Completes the min-max picture of Erdős #76 by pinning the optimum from below at an explicit extremal construction.

proven: Universal upper bound maxPackingSize(c) ≤ C(n,2)/3 ≈ n²/6 for every 2-coloring — parent entry erdos-76-packing-upper-bound (maxPackingSize_le).
Existence of Steiner triple systems STS(k) for k ≡ 1,3 (mod 6) partitioning K_k into C(k,2)/3 edge-disjoint triangles — Kirkman (1847).
Complete bipartite graphs K_{m,m} are triangle-free, so the red class of c_star contributes no triangle.
Gruslys–Letzter (2020): matching universal lower bound ≥ (1+o(1))n²/12 plus a stability result identifying the balanced bipartition as essentially the unique extremal coloring.
open: A formal Lean construction of c_star and a proof that its maximum monochromatic packing is (1+o(1))n²/12.
Combining the parent's n²/6 upper bound with this construction to obtain a self-contained two-sided asymptotic for the specific coloring c_star.
knownResults.goal: Formalize the lower bound for the extremal coloring: construct c_star on Fin n (n even) and prove maxPackingSize(c_star) ≥ (1/12 + o(1))n² by an explicit edge-disjoint blue triangle packing — first the exact Steiner case n/2 ≡ 1,3 (mod 6), then general even n with O(n) deficit.
